findings.regulatory_context: Direct calls to DeepSeek-hosted API endpoints mean prompts and data are sent to infrastructure operated by the excluded vendor. References DHS Exclusion and Removal Order #2026-01 (procurement exclusion of DeepSeek products and services).
findings.remediation: Replace the endpoint with an approved model provider. If the endpoint is only in a comment or dead code, remove it and record the removal in your evidence file.

findings.regulatory_context: A first-party DeepSeek weight file inside the product directory is a DeepSeek implementation artifact in the most literal sense covered by Order #2026-01.
findings.remediation: Remove the weight file from the product and from any image or bundle that embeds it. If weights were renamed, verify provenance with metadata or fingerprint tooling (see the project roadmap) rather than filenames.

findings.regulatory_context: Configuration for the excluded vendor's API indicates an integration point, even if the key itself is not present in the repository.
findings.remediation: Remove the variable from code, examples and deployment configuration. Rotate any real key that was ever committed, then record the change in your evidence file.

findings.rule_name: DeepSeek reference in dependency lockfile (possibly transitive)
findings.regulatory_context: A lockfile hit usually means a transitive (second-hand) dependency pulls in a DeepSeek-related package. Transitive presence still counts as part of the delivered product.
findings.remediation: Trace which top-level dependency pulls it in (your package manager's dependency-tree command), then upgrade, replace or explicitly exclude it and regenerate the lockfile.

limitations:
This scanner checks a fixed, published set of textual and filename indicators. It detects, when present in the scanned tree: references to DeepSeek-hosted API endpoints in source and configuration; DeepSeek SDK imports and package names; DeepSeek names in dependency manifests and lockfiles (direct and transitive); DeepSeek image or model pulls in container definitions; and first-party model weight files and model configs.

It cannot detect: a model distilled from DeepSeek outputs and shipped under a different name with no textual trace; weight files that were renamed and stripped of identifying metadata; calls routed through a third-party gateway under that gateway's own domains and model names; or any use that leaves no artifact in the scanned tree.

A report with findings is evidence that the listed indicators are present at the listed locations. A report without findings means only that none of the indicators in the current rule set were found in the scanned tree; it is not proof that no DeepSeek-derived component exists in a product. Determinations about obligations under DHS Exclusion and Removal Order #2026-01 or FAR 52.204-30 rest with each organization and its counsel. This tool is an evidence-collection aid, not a legal determination.
